result.title: Counterexample-driven autonomous research with application to excess radiated energy in a Z-pinch
result.comment: 25 pages, 9 figures, 5 tables; code at https://github.com/tomzhu0225/simjecture
result.summary: Recent breakthroughs in artificial-intelligence-assisted mathematics show that open-ended machine search can outperform human mathematicians, yet transferring this paradigm to physics requires refactoring the research workflow. We introduce Simjecture, an open-source framework in which language-model agents pursue human-defined physical conjectures. The framework tackles two central challenges in this transfer: first, because physics is empirical and no model is final, it structures inquiry around counterexample-driven falsification and prospective hypothesis repair; second, because physical theories must interact with the real world, it uses computational physics as an executable testbed while separating the qualification of numerical instruments from scientific claim review so solvers and diagnostics can be adapted within a recorded investigation. We apply the framework in an 82.6 h investigation to tackle the long-standing problem of radiated energy exceeding the imploding-shell kinetic energy in a Z-pinch. The investigation reveals competing effects of energy conversion, retention, and release timing. Stronger coherent helical deformation increases resistive conversion while reducing radiation and increasing retained energy. A broader trailing-plasma profile delays the later radiation maximum and recovers much of its early bolometric deficit, with a spectral response that changes during the pulse. These results provide new insight into energy conversion in high-energy-density plasma physics and demonstrate a new paradigm for physics research.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Simjecture 框架，让语言模型智能体围绕人类给定的物理猜想开展研究，以反例驱动的证伪与假设修复组织探索，并用计算物理作为可执行检验环境，在约 82.6 小时内研究 Z-pinch 辐射能量超出内爆壳动能的问题。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「反例驱动证伪＋假设修复」及把数值工具可信度与科学结论审查分离的做法，可能为 LVR 中的验证、停止决策与「视觉证据是否可信」的分离评估提供概念参照，需核查是否真有可迁移机制。
